population: Administrative employees of agri-food companies (Italy per the title; sector, firm size, region, number of firms and agriculture vs food-processing split not reported)
geography: Italy (stated only in the chapter title; no location given in the methods)
ai_definition: Intention to adopt Generative AI (Gen-AI), measured on 5-point Likert items within an integrated TAM-TOE model (constructs: relative advantage, compatibility, top management support, organisational availability, customer pressures, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use, intention to adopt GEN-AI); respondents were given an introduction to Gen-AI. Actual use is not measured.

findings.quote: data was collected through a survey distributed among administrative employees of agri-food companies. A total of 156 respon- dents participated in the survey.
The questionnaire utilized a 5-point Likert scale, ranging from 1 (“completely disagree”) to 5 (“completely agree”).

findings.value: integrated TAM-TOE model of Gen-AI adoption intention
findings.quote: Our research analyses the intention to adopt GEN-AI in the agri-food sector through an integrated model based on the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) [15] and the Technology Organization-Environment model (TOE) [16] constructs.

During the second phase of the study, the collected data was analyzed using the AMOS software. Initially, confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) was conducted to validate the multi-item scales employed in the study [25].

findings.metric: Determinants of Gen-AI adoption intention (qualitative; coefficients only in Fig. 3.2 image, not in text)
findings.value: TAM constructs direct positive; TOE constructs indirect; top management support negative
findings.quote: the intention to adopt Gen-AI in the Agri-food sector is directly influenced by the constructs of TAM and indirectly influenced by the constructs of TOE, except for Top Management Support, which instead has a negative impact
Of particular note is the discernment that merely three out of the 12 hypoth- eses failed to garner empirical support

findings.value: top management support not oriented to Gen-AI adoption
findings.quote: Top Management Support is not completely ori- ented toward the adoption and implementation of GEN-AI in the Agri-food Supply Chain, thus negatively and indirectly influencing the Adoption Intention of the tech- nology.

coi.note: Academic authors (Sapienza University of Rome); no funding or commercial interest declared.

notes: Verified on full text (3 October 2026). Short proceedings chapter (text on PDF pages 1-5, printed pp. 27-31) estimating a TAM-TOE structural model (CFA in AMOS) of the intention to adopt Generative AI on 156 administrative employees of agri-food companies. AI is measured on its own (Gen-AI), but only as adoption intention, not use. Severe limitations: no sampling frame, fieldwork period, region, number of firms, firm size or sector breakdown (farms vs food processing vs logistics) is reported, Italy appears only in the title, path coefficients and fit indices appear only in figures (Figs. 3.1-3.2, not in the text), and the reference list contains evident mis-citations (ref. 15 Davis is a climate paper, ref. 27 Hair is a silica chemistry paper). ELIGIBILITY: recommend EXCLUDE (sector not identifiable: generic agri-food respondents with no food-manufacturing breakdown, Italian location unstated in methods, intention-only evidence); marginal relevance at most for RQ3 (top management support negative) and RQ5 (intention-based Gen-AI measurement).

population: One medium-sized Italian fruit-processing company (Trentofrutta Spa, Trento; 177 employees, turnover about 50 million euro; semi-finished fruit products for industry and contract filling of bottles and pouches), food manufacturing (NACE C10)
ai_definition: No AI-specific measure. Industry 4.0 defined following Russmann et al. (2015) plus blockchain: management software and vertical integration, robotics and IoT in production, an Industry 4.0 plant, 3D printing, big data analytics (production and strategic level), horizontal integration. AI is mentioned only as possible future AI-based food-traceability software, not adopted.

findings.quote: Trentofrutta is a food processing company located in Trento with a factory of 38,000 square meters. With 177 employees and a turnover of about 50 million euro

findings.metric: Own investment in digital transformation and reorganisation, 2015-2021 (Table 1)
findings.quote: Own investments in digital transformation and firm re-organisation (million Euro) 0.7 2.8 4.5 2.4 5.6 1.3 4.2

findings.value: management software and ICT 2015; robotics and IoT; Industry 4.0 plant 2017; big data analytics in the last two years
findings.quote: the digitalisation process started in 2015 with the new management software and information and communication technology systems, followed by advanced robotics and IoT in one plant, a brand-new Industry 4.0 plant in 2017 and big data collection and analytics

findings.value: five-step iterative interviews, May-September 2021, plus archival triangulation
findings.quote: The first in-depth interview was conducted with the Integrated Management System Manager in May 2021. It lasted about 90 min, was recorded and literally transcribed into text.

findings.metric: Effects of the Industry 4.0 plant (self-reported, qualitative)
findings.value: lower average operating cost, partial workforce reduction
findings.quote: Compared to the non-digitalised pouch filling, the Industry 4.0 plant has a lower average operating cost. Automation and digitalisation partially reduced workforce.

findings.metric: Automated quality control in the Industry 4.0 plant
findings.quote: this production plant also includes robots and automatic systems performing 100% controls on quality and hygiene conditions.

findings.value: generational turnover and more female workers
findings.quote: The new hiring procedures, particularly in relation to the Industry 4.0 production plant, resulted into a generational turnover and an increase of female workers.

findings.metric: Big data analytics use in strategy (function)
findings.value: demand forecasting, capacity alignment, risk mitigation
findings.quote: Top management members use big data analytics to better forecast demand trends and align strategic capacity requirements, and, eventually, mitigate risks related to demand decreases and agriculture uncertainty.

findings.value: self-financed; limited public training support and national tax benefits
findings.quote: Apart from limited public support for training and some national tax benefits, the firm self-financed technological investments.

findings.value: uncertainty of outcomes, limited financial resources and digital skills, change resistance, capital-intensive investments, new analytical skills, unprepared suppliers
findings.quote: Limited financial resources and digital skills

findings.metric: AI not adopted: AI traceability software only prospective (qualitative)
findings.quote: Although there are already Artificial Intelligence-based software products specifically developed for food traceability, this approach would require an additional cultural change in the organisation and within the supply chain.
This single case study has an exploratorypurpose, rather than generalisability of findings.

notes: Verified on full text (3 October 2026). Single exploratory case study (interviews May-September 2021 plus archival data) of Trentofrutta, a medium Italian fruit-processing firm (food manufacturing, NACE C10), describing drivers, barriers, strategies and self-reported outcomes of incremental Industry 4.0 adoption since 2015 (management software, robotics and IoT, an Industry 4.0 pouch-filling plant, 3D printing, big data analytics). AI is not measured: big data analytics is adopted, while AI-based traceability software is only mentioned as a future option requiring cultural change. Limitations: n=1 purposively chosen success case, qualitative self-reported outcomes, no counterfactual. ELIGIBILITY: INCLUDE (Italian peer-reviewed Industry 4.0 adoption evidence from one food-manufacturing firm). Relevance: RQ3 (top-management vision, group ICT resources, self-financing, skills and change resistance), RQ2 (BDA for planning and strategy), RQ4 (qualitative cost, productivity and workforce-composition effects).
